item.title: Netizen Voices: Latest Birthrate Stats Suggest That “When More Grown-ups Weep, Fewer Babies Wail”
item.description: Demographic data released by China’s National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) on Monday revealed that in 2025, China’s population fell for a fourth consecutive year, and the annual birthrate plummeted below eight million, a record low. The news prompted a flurry of online comments and articles, and some censorship of the topic on social media platforms. […]

item.title: Suppressing the Memory of June 4: Tiananmen Mothers’ New Year Gathering Blocked in Beijing; Vigil Organizers on Trial in Hong Kong
item.description: On January 15, non-governmental organization Human Rights in China (HRIC) reported that, for the first time, the Chinese government obstructed the annual New Year’s gathering of the Tiananmen Mothers. item.title: CDT’s “404 Deleted Content Archive” Summary for December 2025, Part One
item.description: CDT presents a monthly series of censored content that has been added to our “404 Deleted Content Archive.” Each month, we publish a summary of content blocked or deleted (often yielding the message “404: content not found”) from Chinese platforms such as WeChat, Weibo, Douyin (TikTok’s counterpart in the Chinese market), Xiaohongshu (RedNote), Bilibili, Zhihu, […]

item.title: Translation: “They’re Just Cutting Everything Down Indiscriminately.” Positivity on Birth Rate Doesn’t Keep Censors at Bay
item.description: Recent figures from China’s National Bureau of Statistics showed that despite policies ranging from childcare subsidies to reported menstrual monitoring, the country saw a fourth consecutive year of population decline and fewer than eight million births—roughly equal to the level in 1738.
